017de30f8525bdceea9bd3e3018692cc2131971d: Arolla is a small, low-key resort with 27 km of runs, offering an intimate skiing experience far from the bustle of the big resorts. It's the place to come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Arolla's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It's one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. With a summit at 2877 m and a village at 1984 m, snow reliability at Arolla is generally good from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause difficulties early in the season, but conditions usually recover quickly once the first heavy snowfalls arrive. Budgeting for a stay in Arolla is clearly on the high side: 53€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you go. In short, Arolla doesn't rival the giants of skiing and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest, often underrated destination that deserves to be (re)discovered.

019744bac06bcc177c808509d886e92b3817576a: Aprica is a resort on a human scale, focusing on friendly welcome and proximity rather than impressive figures. Its 50 km of runs suit a stay of 3 to 4 days perfectly, especially for families or skiers who don't need to constantly change their playground. Aprica's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a relaxed, friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Aprica's altitude (1162 m at the base, 2270 m at the top) helps it maintain decent snow cover in mid-winter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it's worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. Spending a week in Aprica is clearly on the expensive side: 57€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but it's worth being aware of it before you go. In short: Aprica keeps its promises. A Northern Alps resort that will suit most types of skier without disappointing.
